title: Koine desktop contract
intro: Koine's desktop contract as built: one resident Koine application, a shared resilient Swift provider framework and bearer credentials with live revocation. These views explain its boundaries and ordering. "Agreed" in a diagram marks the contract the human approved, which the implementation follows; what has been verified, and what is still open, is the spec's "Test seams and acceptance".

discussion.title: Retained AX objects do not preserve process incarnation
discussion.status: Server-private API investigation authorized; strict lifetime preserved
discussion.summary: On macOS 26.5, an old retained AX window minimized a replacement process at recycled PID 781. The holder kept its original task-name right and AX parent and performed no fresh AX acquisition. A separate observer confirmed the effect. The human chose to investigate private APIs inside Koine while keeping client APIs public and preserving strict process lifetime. This authorizes investigation, not a particular mechanism, restart policy or replacement schema.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Added the actual PID-reuse counterexample: a held AX window acts on a replacement process while the original task right is dead.

diagrams.title: Why retained AX objects do not bind native effects
diagrams.caption: Actual PID reuse in a disposable macOS 26.5 TestAnyware VM, with a controlled Cocoa app. The holder never reacquired AX objects after the original process ended. It intentionally used the retained window after death to test endpoint lifetime; this is not an observed Koine mistarget. Separate observers saw the replacement before and after minimization. Source, frozen-input hashes, output and limitations are in docs/verification/retained-ax-binding.md. Server-private investigation is authorized; a particular private dependency, native protocol or weaker action guarantee is not approved.

diagrams.title: Why a public serial cannot identify the process
diagrams.caption: Observed in a macOS 26.5 TestAnyware clone with a diagnostic app. The same serial and boot identity resolved to PID 893, continued to report that PID after the process ended, then resolved to live PID 910 after automatic restoration. Captured sources, hashes and native output are in docs/verification/process-serial-lifetime.md. The human requires expiry with the original process, so PSN plus boot identity is ruled out. This does not establish unrelated-application serial reuse, actual PID reuse, or native Accessibility action safety.

diagrams.title: Capture at the server or at the client event
diagrams.caption: Client-event capture and strict OS-process lifetime are agreed. Server-side capture can select another application after an intervening app switch and is rejected. Transferring a retained task right is the next candidate, not a completed protocol: port numbers are local names, rights do not reserve PIDs, and capture attribution, native endpoint binding, authentication, reference non-reuse and restart policy must be specified. The existing Desktop interaction view remains context for the served contract.

diagrams.title: Resident application and client boundary
diagrams.caption: Agreed runtime responsibility view: one resident Koine application contains the native UI, server and providers. Closing its management window leaves the listener and observation running. The native UI keeps management authority in process; HTTP clients present bearer credentials backed by live grants. Providers share that process and its OS permissions. The shared resilient Swift framework is agreed.

diagrams.title: Source packages and interface dependencies
diagrams.caption: Agreed application/framework composition, shown as package dependencies rather than deployment containers. Koine supplies one shared provider framework image, Machine invokes its contracts, and separately built providers conform to them. Published Swift types and protocols carry the compatibility promise; GraphQL-library types remain private. The client owns its GraphQL adapter; no Koine-owned client helper is required for this deliverable.

diagrams.title: Discover windows, derive choices, focus one
diagrams.caption: Agreed end-to-end sequence. The client captures the process incarnation at interaction start, queries before deriving choices, then submits the selected opaque reference. The provider re-resolves it before native focus and reports unavailable for a closed, stale or ambiguous target. Remembered observations can outlive current visibility; they are not an atomic snapshot. Capability denial and missing Koine OS consent have separate machine-readable classifications.

diagrams.title: Authorize every action before executing any
diagrams.caption: Agreed execution flow for an authenticated client operation. The core expands the selected GraphQL operation and checks original schema coordinates, so aliases and fragments do not rename authority. Any denied mutation action prevents all actions from beginning. Revocation is checked again at each dispatch admission. Earlier authorized effects are not rolled back if a later action fails. Enrollment and the in-process console have separately defined admission cases in the spec.

diagrams.title: Grant issuance, approval and revocation
diagrams.caption: Agreed bearer-credential lifecycle and revocation ordering. Anonymous enrollment creates only a pending request. Existing managers or the in-process console approve requests or create manual grants. Approved grants survive restart without automatic expiry; pending-request expiry does not expire them. Secret possession permits own-request status before and after its decision; revoked grants fail authentication. Digest uniqueness prevents retries from creating multiple grants. Already admitted actions may finish. This diagram is not a model-checking result.

diagrams.title: Agreed Swift framework and the alternative
diagrams.caption: The human selected the shared resilient Swift framework. Swift types and protocols are part of its stable published contract, with library evolution and module stability enabled from release one. The C-compatible alternative is not selected. Compatible provider binaries dynamically link the host-supplied framework; newer required symbols need a newer host and are checked before loading.

diagrams.title: Native schema and resolver contributions
diagrams.caption: The shared Swift framework as the loader applies it. Verify signed manifests and required framework versions before loading, then resolve the named principal class and require ProviderFactory conformance. Validate schema and authority metadata before starting the Provider. Requests/results use owned Swift values and async protocol methods. Independently built old/new binaries are verified through the native plugin seam (docs/verification/binary-compatibility.md); native trust is distinct from client capabilities.
